THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO QUASH THE IMPUGNED ORDER DATED 15.05.2023 PASSED ON THE INTERLOCUTORY APPLICATION FILED BY PETITIONER UNDER ORDER 18 RULE 17 R/W SECTION 151 OF CPC IN MVC NO 969/2022 PASSED BY THE VII ADDITIONAL JUDGE AND ACMM, (MACT),
(SCCH-3), AT BENGALURU VIDE ANNEURE-A AND ETC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This petition by the claimant in MVC No.969/2022 is directed against the impugned order dated 15.05.2023, whereby the application filed by the petitioner/claimant under Order 18 Rule 17 of CPC was rejected by the trial Court.

The material on record discloses that in the aforesaid claim petition filed by the petitioner claimant seeking compensation towards the injuries sustained by him in an alleged road traffic accident said to have occurred on 23.03.2021, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and was cross-examined by the respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Subsequent thereto, the petitioner filed the instant application NC: 2023:KHC:20820 seeking to recall the stage and for permission to re-examine the petitioner/PW.1 by recalling him.

The said application having been orally opposed by the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company, the trial Court proceeded to pass the impugned order rejecting the application, aggrieved by which, the petitioner is before this Court by way of the present petition.

2. A perusal of the material on record indicates that the sole ground on which the trial Court has rejected the application is that there was an admission in the cross examination of PW.1 which cannot be taken away by virtue of re-examining himself or by adducing further evidence.

In this context, the trial Court has entirely pre-judged the issue as regards the credibility and veracity of evidence of PW.1 without appreciating the fact that these are compensation proceedings arising out Sri S T Puttaswamy vs Sri Ravi M on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95240246/
2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which is a beneficial piece of legislation and the evidentiary value and the effect of admissions made in the cross examination of a party would necessarily lie in realm of appreciation of evidence, which would have to be considered at the time of final disposal of the suit and not at the stage of permitting a party to adduce further evidence, either by recalling himself or adducing further evidence.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, I am of the view, that the impugned order 15.05.2023 passed by the trial Court deserves to be set aside and liberty is granted to the petitioner/claimant.
Petitioner be permitted to recall himself as PW.1 to adduce further evidence.

In the result the following :-
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned order dated 15.05.2023 is set aside.
The application stands disposed of, by permitting the petitioner/PW.1 to adduce further evidence on his side.
iii. All rival contentions on all aspects of both the parties are kept open without expressing any opinion on the same.
